preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Attacker must hold some CHC tokens to demonstrate fee impact

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call setBurnFee() and setSwapFee() with excessively high values (e.g., 99). Then perform a token transfer to/from the swapAddress to trigger the fee mechanism, causing disproportionate token burns and liquidity fees that benefit the owner-controlled addresses.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The CitysHome token contract allows the owner to set excessively high burn and swap fees (up to 99%). When the swapAddress is involved in transfers, fees are applied. The owner can set swapAddress to their own address, then perform transfers where swapAddress is the sender, collecting the liquidity fees to themselves while burning tokens from other users. This creates an economic imbalance where the owner can extract value from token holders.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Set swapAddress to attacker address. 3. Set both burnFee and liquidityFee to 99 (99%). 4. Get some CHC tokens from the contract's reserve using ownerWithdrew. 5. Transfer tokens from swapAddress (attacker) to another address, triggering the fee mechanism where liquidity fees go back to swapAddress (attacker). 6. The attacker's balance increases due to receiving liquidity fees.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Start prank as owner. 2. Call setSwapAddress(attacker). 3. Call setBurnFee(99) and setSwapFee(99). 4. Call ownerWithdrew to get initial tokens from contract reserve. 5. Create a dummy recipient address. 6. Transfer tokens from attacker (as swapAddress) to dummy recipient. 7. This triggers the fee logic where liquidity fees (99% of amount) go back to swapAddress (attacker). 8. Stop prank and verify attacker balance increased.
